tools.description:

Takes the citation in the form you already hold it — including the court name, the dispositive word and the date a model normally writes around a docket. KEEP THEM IN: the court

tools.name: listCasePassages
tools.description:
The full text of one decision, split into its paragraphs, each with a permalink you can cite.

`rn` is the Randnummer the COURT printed, read out of the decision's own markup. It is never inferred from position: where a document prints no numbers, `rn` is null and stays null. `anchor_basis` is deriv

tools.name: getChanges
tools.description:
Which provisions got a new text recently, newest first — the freshness feed, as JSON. Poll it with `since` set to the newest `observed` you have already processed.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "resolveIdentifiers" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: resolveIdentifiers, getNorm, listCitingDecisions · Private data: search, listCasePassages · Public sink: resolveIdentifiers · Destructive: listCasePassages.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: resolveIdentifiers, getNorm, listCitingDecisions · Private data: search, listCasePassages · Public sink: resolveIdentifiers · Destructive: listCasePassages

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
